lanes.summary: The diff successfully fulfills the second part of PMAT-3718 ('serve usage and finish_reason never report a cut as a stop') by replacing all instances of hardcoded `"stop"` finish reasons with `finish_reason_for(tokens_generated, max_tokens)` in `serve` contexts (including `chat.rs`, `handlers.rs`, and `handler_gpu_completion.rs`), ensuring they correctly report `"length"` when a generation is cut off. It also correctly bounds `max_tokens` with `context_token_budget` to avoid `wgpu` returning `"stop"` for a full context window cutoff. The `apr run --json` requirements from the ticket's title were absent in this diff, but since the ticket is 50% complete, they were verified to exist in a prior commit (`run_tests_usage_3718.rs`). No ticket constraints were violated.

lanes.summary: The diff fixes the "serve … never report a cut as a stop" half of PMAT-3718 (the "apr run --json" half was already merged to main in a prior commit, consistent with the 50% progress marker). It introduces `finish_reason_for(generated, max_tokens)` → "length" when generated ≥ max_tokens, else "stop" — and wires it into the four serve paths that previously hardcoded "stop": (1) wgpu non-streaming, (2) wgpu streaming done-chunk, (3) CUDA non-streaming, (4) CUDA→CPU fallback, and (5) SafeTensors chat. Context-budget refusal for wgpu (done_when 3) is also plumbed. One receipt claim is slightly overstated — the commit message says "All four serve paths now take finish_reason from ONE rule" but the CPU-path streaming handler (`handler_apr_cpu_completion.rs:280`) still has its own inline `if n >= ctx.max_tokens { "length" } else { "stop" }` rather than calling `finish_reason_for`. However, the logic is semantically identical and the file is untouched by this diff, so it is not a regression or a gate weakening — just an aspirational claim about consolidation that doesn't match reality. No tests assert the opposite of the ticket. No gates are weakened. The diff does nothing the ticket forbids.

findings.claim: finish_reason_for returns "length" when generated >= max_tokens and "stop" otherwise, matching the ticket requirement that a cut is never reported as a stop.

Test a_reply_that_used_the_whole_budget_is_length_not_stop asserts finish_reason_for(64,64)=="length", finish_reason_for(65,64)=="length", finish_reason_for(63,64)=="stop", finish_reason_for(0,64)=="stop" — consistent with ticket.
New test a_reply_cut_at_max_tokens_is_length_not_stop passes tokens_generated=16, max_tokens=16 and asserts finish_reason is "length", exercising the SafeTensors path.
CUDA non-streaming path now uses finish_reason_for(tokens_generated, max_tokens_clamped) instead of hardcoded "stop".
CUDA→CPU fallback now uses finish_reason_for(out.tokens_generated, max_tokens) instead of hardcoded "stop".
wgpu streaming done-chunk now uses finish_reason_for(completion_tokens as usize, max_tokens) instead of hardcoded "stop".
wgpu non-streaming path replaces its inline if/else with finish_reason_for(output_ids.len(), max_tokens), consolidating to the shared rule.
wgpu_chat_completion now calls context_token_budget before prefill, refusing prompts ≥ context_length with HTTP 400 and an OpenAI-shaped error body (done_when 3).

The commit message claims 'All four serve paths now take finish_reason from ONE rule, finish_reason_for' but this file's streaming path still has its own inline `if n >= ctx.max_tokens { "length" } else { "stop" }` — semantically identical but not calling finish_reason_for. The claim is aspirational, not backed by the diff, but the logic is correct and pre-existing.
The CUDA SSE streaming path (build_gpu_sse_stream) sends [DONE] without a finish_reason chunk. This is pre-existing, not introduced by the diff, and not a regression.
